Auspicious

aw-SPISH-us -- stress on the second syllable, SPISH. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Auspicious is showing signs that promise a good future.

A record crowd on opening night was an auspicious sign for the theater's new season.

Worked Example

On the exchange student's very first morning, her host family greets her in her own language, the sun breaks a week of rain, and her new school assigns the one novel she already loves.

Everything about that first day is auspicious: each detail reads like a sign that the whole year ahead will go well. Auspicious belongs to beginnings, omens, and starts that point toward success.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

promising: showing signs of future success

favorable: advantageous; working in one's favor

propitious: indicating a strong chance of success

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

ominous: suggesting that something bad is coming

inauspicious: boding ill; unpromising

Where it sits · how strongly success seems guaranteed — favorable → auspicious → propitious

favorable vs. auspicious: Favorable is milder and more matter-of-fact -- favorable conditions simply help, while an auspicious start feels like an omen, hinting that fortune itself has taken your side.

propitious vs. auspicious: Propitious presses the promise even further than auspicious: an auspicious sign suggests things will go well, while a propitious moment practically guarantees it -- the stars aligned, the timing perfect, success all but assured.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — auspic-

root — auspic-: divination by watching birds (Latin auspicium, from avis 'bird' + specere 'to look at')

suffix — -ious

suffix — -ious: full of; possessing the qualities of (Latin -osus, via Old French -ous)

Put it together

Put it together: Auspicious uses the -ious variant of this unit's suffix family. Latin auspicium was 'bird-watching' of a very special kind: Roman priests read the flight of birds -- avis ('bird') plus specere ('to look at') -- to predict whether an undertaking would succeed. Something auspicious is literally 'full of good bird-omens': the signs at the start all point to success.

Use the root in a new word: inspect

Use the root in a new word: inspect: The mechanic inspected the brakes carefully before the family's long road trip.

Root Check

Word Choice

Auspicious clings to beginnings and signs: an auspicious start, an auspicious debut, an auspicious omen, an auspicious date for a wedding. It is odd to call a sandwich or a chair auspicious -- the word needs a future to point at. Its built-in opposite, inauspicious, marks the start that bodes ill.
